calculations.title: Frame-Explicit D-Plane Geometry and Rate-of-Closure Adaptation

inputs.name: face_normal
inputs.basis: Delivered face-normal direction in the declared target frame.

inputs.name: target
inputs.basis: Positive target direction; orthogonal to up.

inputs.name: travel_vector
inputs.basis: Club reference, face-center, or contact-point velocity; only direction enters geometry.
inputs.valid_range: Any finite vector; norm at or below 1e-12 returns zero_travel

inputs.name: up
inputs.basis: Positive vertical direction; orthogonal to target.

outputs.name: face_to_path_deg
outputs.basis: Wrapped face heading minus club-path heading.

outputs.name: spin_loft_3d_deg
outputs.basis: Principal angle between travel and face-normal unit vectors.

preconditions: All supplied vectors contain exactly three finite components.
Face normal, target, and up have norms greater than 1e-12.
Target and up are orthogonal within an absolute dot-product tolerance of 1e-10.
postconditions: Defined direction outputs are unit length within floating-point precision.
Spin loft is the clipped principal angle in [0, 180] degrees.
Singular states retain available face orientation and do not fabricate a D-plane axis.
invariants: A common proper rotation preserves intrinsic angular metrics.
Right-left reflection reverses signed horizontal relationships and preserves spin loft.
Velocity magnitude does not change geometric outputs when travel direction is unchanged.
failure_modes: Malformed, non-finite, zero face/axis, or non-orthogonal frame inputs raise ValueError.
Zero travel returns zero_travel with direction-dependent outputs set to null.
Parallel and antiparallel vectors return typed singular states without a fabricated normal.

equations.description: Right axis and signed target-frame headings.
Normalized cross product defining the D-plane normal.
Principal three-dimensional angle between travel and face normal.

numerical_method.algorithm: Finite 3-vector validation, Euclidean normalization, clipped dot-product inverse cosine, cross products, atan2 headings/elevations, and typed singular-state branching.
numerical_method.fallback_policy: No numerical or physical estimate is substituted. Zero, parallel, antiparallel, and unprojectable states expose explicit null outputs.

limitations: The calculation is geometry only; it does not infer launch direction, spin magnitude, aerodynamic curvature, or equipment performance.
The default frame convention is a software contract, not a claim that an external sensor already uses that frame.
The Rate-of-Closure adapter reports reference, face-center, and contact analyses separately; downstream flight currently consumes reference-point translation.
Scientific, rendered-page, accessibility, and human approval remain outstanding.
